title: Bench-to-Belong: Playbook for Rotational and Short-Term Hires — Onboarding, Manager Guidance, and Feedback
author: Elena Park
body:
Overview:
This playbook ('Bench-to-Belong') describes the standard process, manager responsibilities, and evaluation checkpoints for rotational hires, contractors on conversion tracks, and short-term internal transfers at Redwood. It covers intake decisions, a condensed 90-day onramp curriculum, structured feedback cadences, conversion evaluation, and escalation paths. The goal is to reduce time-to-impact while providing consistent fairness and technical calibration across teams.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: rotational hires (0-6 month rotations), contractors on a path to full-time, internal short-term transfers (<=6 months).
- Primary audience: hiring managers, people ops partners, team leads, onboarding buddies, and hiring panel members.

Definitions:
- Rotational hire: a candidate placed for a defined rotation (often for learning) with a formal end or conversion decision.
- Conversion track: contractor / IC with explicit criteria + evaluation window for offer to full-time.
- Bench-to-belong: program term used internally to describe intentional conversion & integration activities.

Owner and SLAs:
- Playbook owner: People Ops (owner: Elena Park).
- Manager SLA: complete role-specific onboarding checklist within 5 business days of start; first probation calibration meeting scheduled within 10 business days.

High-level process (summary):
1) Hiring intake & offer kickoff
   - People Ops creates a role intake form (link template in appendix) that must include: rotation length, conversion eligibility, key measurable outcomes, mentor/buddy assignment, and security requirements.
2) Preboarding (before day 1)
   - Access requests: manager initiates access ticket to infra and code repos (see matrix below).
   - Welcome packet: manager sends role brief, 30/60/90 editable goals, and first-week schedule.
3) Day 0–7 (orientation and systems)
   - Core orientation: company intro, compliance modules, and service map walkthrough.
   - First-week pairing: buddy pairing and 3 shallow onboarding tasks to verify access.
4) Day 8–30 (skill onramp)
   - Role-specific shadowing, small scoped deliverables, and first written feedback from manager.
5) Day 31–60 (independent contribution)
   - Measurable deliverable 1 and mid-point conversion checkpoint.
6) Day 61–90 (final assessment)
   - Final deliverable, conversion recommendation, and calibration meeting with People Ops.

Manager responsibilities (checklist):
- Pre-start: complete role intake; confirm mentor and workspace; submit access tickets (SLA: 5 business days pre-start).
- Day 0–7: hold onboarding 1:1 cadenced daily or every-other-day; run welcome tour; ensure initial tickets tasks exist.
- Week 2: submit initial assessment note in HRIS (template in appendix).
- Week 4: schedule & run 30-day check-in using the structured rubric.
- Week 8: submit conversion recommendation (pass/extend/fail) with evidence and deliverables.
- Week 12: finalize conversion decision; if offering FT, provide written offer and compensation rationale; loop People Ops to execute.

Structured 90-day microcurriculum (example):
- Week 0–1: Orientation + infra access + low-risk tasks (DOC, README edits, small bug fixes).
- Week 2–4: Paired work + one scoped feature or triage deliverable.
- Week 5–8: Independent ownership of a slice of work + code review throughput target (e.g., 4 PRs).
- Week 9–12: Final deliverable with written design doc or customer-impact writeup and presentation to the team.

Feedback cadence & templates:
- Day 3 'Access & Engagement' quick sync (10–20m): verify tooling and social connections.
- Week 2 'Initial Readout' 1:1 (30m): manager to provide 3 strengths and 2 short growth areas.
- Week 4 '30-day' formal check-in (45m): use the Evaluation Rubric (table below) and set updated 30/60 goals.
- Week 8 'Midpoint' written note: manager uploads midterm evidence to HRIS + optional calibration meeting.
- Week 12 'Final' formal assessment (60m): discuss recommendation and next steps.

One-line manager 1:1 agenda template (Week 4 / Week 12):
- Quick wins (5m)
- Roadblocks & support needed (10m)
- Evidence review: deliverables, PRs, peer feedback (15m)
- Career / conversion conversation (10–20m)

Evaluation Rubric (use for 30/60/90 checks):
- Categories (score 1-5): Technical execution, Collaboration & communication, Ownership & proactivity, Reliability & timeliness, Learning velocity.
- Scoring guidance:
  - 5 = Exceeds expectations for role and remit
  - 4 = Solidly meets expectations with occasional stretch
  - 3 = Meets baseline expectations
  - 2 = Needs structured coaching
  - 1 = Significant gaps; remedial plan required

Example table (plain text) — manager completes numeric scores + evidence:
- Technical execution: 4 — wrote two PRs, passed unit tests, reviewer feedback positive.
- Collaboration: 3 — good cross-team communication, needs more async docs.
- Ownership: 4 — proactively took bug triage lead for sprint.

Conversion decision rules (recommended):
- Pass: average score >= 3.7 and no single category < 3; evidence of ownership and at least one cross-team positive peer note.
- Extend (30 days): average score between 3.0 and 3.6 or single category = 2; requires an explicit development plan.
- Fail: average score < 3.0 or any category = 1 with unremediated gaps after extension.

Calibration & fairness safeguards:
- All conversion recommendations must be reviewed by People Ops and one peer reviewer from another team for cross-team bias reduction.
- For any recommended fail or extend decisions, a calibration meeting with People Ops and the manager must occur within 5 business days of the decision.
- Managers must document the objective evidence (PR links, demo notes, peer messages) supporting their recommendation.

Access matrix (minimum items — manager to request as applicable):
- Code repo: read/write (scoped branch) — SLA: 3 business days
- Cloud console (view): role-based view — SLA: 5 business days
- Internal wiki: read — immediate (auto)
- CI/CD preview runner: access on request — SLA: 7 business days

Sample email templates (shortened):
- Preboarding welcome (sent by manager):
  Subject: Welcome to [Team]! Your Day 1 plan
  Body: Hi [Name], welcome — attached: first-week schedule, buddy intro, 30/60/90 draft. Please complete compliance modules before Day 2.

- Midpoint check-in invite:
  Subject: 30/60/90 mid-check + deliverables review
  Body: Hi [Name], let’s review progress on deliverables and agree next actions. Please upload demo link and a 1-paragraph summary beforehand.

Escalations and exceptions:
- If access is not provisioned by SLA, manager escalates to infra-sre@redwood.com and copies People Ops.
- If a conversion decision is contested, People Ops opens an appeal process: appoint a neutral reviewer from the same level and run a 7-business-day evidence review.

Success metrics (people-ops cares):
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (target: <= 21 days)
- Fraction of rotational hires converted to FT within 120 days (target: >= 55%)
- Manager satisfaction score with onboarding toolkit (target: >= 4.2 / 5)
- Candidate experience NPS (target: >= +50)

Reporting and dashboards:
- People Ops will publish a monthly rotational hires dashboard (metrics above + conversion reasons). Managers must update HRIS milestones within 3 business days of each checkpoint.

Playbook exceptions and special cases:
- Regulated roles: include security review during intake; longer evaluation windows allowed (up to 180 days).
- Customer-facing hires: require references and at least one recorded customer demo before conversion pass.

Appendix A — Templates and links:
- Role intake form (People Ops template): /confluence/people-ops/templates/role-intake-rotations
- HRIS evaluation note template: /confluence/people-ops/templates/hris-eval-note
- Offer checklist and compensation guidance: /confluence/people-ops/comp-and-bands-review-playbook-and-merit-process-2026

Appendix B — Manager quick references (one-pagers):
- Week-by-week 90-day checklist (printable)
- Feedback phrases to use in early development conversations
- Hiring biases checklist for conversion decisions

Versioning and updates:
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly. Submit suggested changes via the People Ops playbook PR process (link in appendix).

Contact and ownership:
- People Ops (playbook owner): Elena Park — people-ops@redwood.com
- For infra access SLA questions: infra-sre@redwood.com

Notes and rationale:
- Bench-to-Belong emphasizes measurable deliverables and lightweight, time-boxed evaluation to avoid long probation ambiguity while ensuring fairness and calibration. The playbook balances manager autonomy with People Ops oversight for consistency across teams.
